\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{باغ} (bâgh)}{باغ (bâgh)}]{\fa{باغ} (bâgh) — a garden; an orchard}

\label{lesson:FA-C467-bagh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a pasture, then the Persian for to graze.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{باغ}}
\textbf{\fa{باغ}} (\emph{bâgh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a garden; an orchard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خانه} \fa{پدربزرگم} \fa{یک} \fa{باغ} \fa{بزرگ} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khâne-ye pedarbozorgam yek bâgh-e bozorg dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather's house has a big garden.
\end{quote}

The Persian garden, with water and trees in a walled square, is famous.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâgh} is inherited: EtymDB traces it to Middle Persian \emph{bāg} 'garden, orchard'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâgh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâgh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâgh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a pasture, then the Persian for to graze, then say \emph{bâgh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{باغ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A garden; an orchard\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{باغچه} (bâghche)}{باغچه (bâghche)}]{\fa{باغچه} (bâghche) — a flower bed, a small garden (in a courtyard)}

\label{lesson:FA-C467-baghche}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to graze, then the Persian for a garden.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{باغچه}}
\textbf{\fa{باغچه}} (\emph{bâghche}) — \textquotedblleft{}a flower bed, a small garden (in a courtyard)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{در} \fa{باغچه} \fa{حیاط} \fa{گل} \fa{کاشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâdaram dar bâghche-ye hayât gol kâsht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother planted flowers in the courtyard bed.
\end{quote}

\emph{bâgh} + \emph{-che} 'little'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâghche} is a native word, which EtymDB lists with the sense 'small garden'; it is built from \emph{bâgh} 'garden' and \emph{-che} 'little'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to graze, then the Persian for a garden, then say \emph{bâghche} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{باغبان} (bâghbân)}{باغبان (bâghbân)}]{\fa{باغبان} (bâghbân) — a gardener}

\label{lesson:FA-C467-baghban}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a garden, then the Persian for a flower bed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{باغبان}}
\textbf{\fa{باغبان}} (\emph{bâghbân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a gardener\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{باغبان} \fa{درختهای} \fa{باغ} \fa{را} \fa{آب} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bâghbân derakht-hâ-ye bâgh râ âb dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The gardener watered the trees in the garden.
\end{quote}

\emph{bâgh} + \emph{-bân} 'keeper', as in \emph{negahbân}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâghbân} is a native compound of \emph{bâgh} 'garden', from Middle Persian \emph{bāg} (EtymDB), and \emph{-bân} 'keeper', as in \emph{negahbân} 'guard'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâghbân}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a garden, then the Persian for a flower bed, then say \emph{bâghbân} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چمن} (chaman)}{چمن (chaman)}]{\fa{چمن} (chaman) — grass, a lawn}

\label{lesson:FA-C467-chaman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a flower bed, then the Persian for a gardener.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{چمن}}
\textbf{\fa{چمن}} (\emph{chaman}) — \textquotedblleft{}grass, a lawn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{روی} \fa{چمن} \fa{فوتبال} \fa{بازی} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bachche-hâ ru-ye chaman futbâl bâzi kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children played football on the grass.
\end{quote}

Also an old word for a meadow in poetry.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{chaman} is a native word, which EtymDB lists with the senses 'lawn, meadow'. Its older form is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chaman}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chaman}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{chaman}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a flower bed, then the Persian for a gardener, then say \emph{chaman} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هرس} \fa{کردن} (haras kardan)}{هرس کردن (haras kardan)}]{\fa{هرس} \fa{کردن} (haras kardan) — to prune}

\label{lesson:FA-C467-haras-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a gardener, then the Persian for grass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هرس} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{هرس} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{haras kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to prune\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{باغبان} \fa{در} \fa{زمستان} \fa{درختها} \fa{را} \fa{هرس} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bâghbân dar zemestân derakht-hâ râ haras mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The gardener prunes the trees in winter.
\end{quote}

\emph{haras} 'pruning' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{haras kardan} is built from \emph{haras} 'pruning', whose origin is not settled, and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haras kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{haras kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a gardener, then the Persian for grass, then say \emph{haras kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 460–467 — a review}

(\textbf{\fa{معامله} \fa{کردن}}.) A down payment? (\textbf{\fa{بیعانه}}.) To overcharge? (\textbf{\fa{گران} \fa{فروختن}}.) A farm? (\textbf{\fa{مزرعه}}.) Wheat? (\textbf{\fa{گندم}}.) A rice paddy?
